plain_english_policy: This bill imposes a three-year pause (moratorium) on both imposing new death sentences and carrying out executions in Alabama. During this time, the state must implement specific reforms to ensure fairness: adopting American Bar Association guidelines for defense counsel, strengthening post-conviction relief processes, eliminating racial discrimination in sentencing based on the victim or defendant's race, and preventing the execution of individuals who are mentally retarded (intellectually disabled) or were under 18 at the time of their crime.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would immediately halt all death penalty activities for three years while mandating procedural reforms aimed at reducing wrongful convictions and racial bias in capital cases before executions could resume.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill's sponsors affirmatively advanced a policy of pausing the death penalty to implement fairness reforms.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would place a moratorium on the death penalty for a period of three years until certain procedures are implemented to ensure that death penalty cases are administered fairly and impartially."
"There shall be a moratorium of three years on the imposition or execution, or both, of the death penalty..."
